contract_conformance.notes: Every Phase 0 contract has live tests AND end-to-end proof on the wire. src/shared/schemas.ts exposes PingInputSchema / PingResponseSchema / ScanEventSchema, src/shared/ipc.ts exposes IPC.SYSTEM.PING and PRELOAD_BRIDGE_KEY 'atr', and src/shared/types.ts re-exports v1 entity types unchanged. 35 schema unit tests pass (tests/unit/shared/schemas.spec.ts). The backend agent shipped the pure handler `handlePing(raw): Promise<PingResponse>` as required, so the 9/9 conformance tests in tests/unit/main/ipc/system.spec.ts now PASS (previously 7 passing + 2 skipped). The Playwright Electron E2E (tests/e2e/electron-launch.spec.ts) launched the packaged app, observed the main window, asserted 'pong' was rendered into the renderer, and asserted a numeric mainProcessPid round-tripped — that's the smoking gun that the IPC contract works through preload + contextBridge + main, not just at the schema layer.

test_coverage.notes: Phase 0 specific: 44 tests passing (35 schema + 9 IPC conformance), 0 skipped, 0 failed. Suite-wide: 66 passing + 5 skipped + 2 env-bound failures (tests/git/scanner.test.ts — see issues[]). Playwright Electron E2E PASSES (1 passed in 4.2s) end-to-end. The native-rebuild dance is solved — `electron-builder install-app-deps` moved out of `postinstall` into a dedicated `electron:rebuild` script chained into electron:dev / electron:pack / electron:dist, so `pnpm test` now runs cleanly against host-Node-built natives. Not a 5 because the two scanner tests are still red against the current host (1Password SSH/GPG signing breaks simple-git temp-repo commits) — pre-existing flake outside Phase 0 scope, documented in issues[].

security.notes: All Phase 0 IPC payloads run through Zod at the contract boundary; the live handlePing exercised in unit tests asserts the parse-then-respond invariant, and the contract document (contracts/ipc.v1.md) requirement to validate event.senderFrame.url is encoded in test expectations. By inspection of the now-authored src/main/index.ts and src/preload/index.ts: contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true, nodeIntegration: false, strict CSP applied, sender-frame allowlist + URL check enforced before any handler executes. ELECTRON_DISABLE_SECURITY_WARNINGS is set only by the Playwright test runner, never in production. Not a 5 because we have not yet added an automated test that the production build refuses to load a non-allowlisted file:// URL — recommended for Phase 1.

code_quality.notes: Strict-TS clean across new code (tsc --noEmit passes). The carried-over implicit-any at lib/github/client.ts:224 was fixed by the infra fix agent. No `expect(true).toBe(true)` placeholders — every test has real assertions. Vitest config supports legacy + Phase 0 globs without losing legacy paths. Playwright Electron config is isolated from the Next.js playwright config so neither suite stomps the other. Wrapper script scripts/run-electron-e2e.mjs has clean error messages and a --skip-build escape hatch. Not a 5 because no `pnpm lint` pass was attempted in this gate run — strict TS is honored but ESLint surface is uninspected.

issues.description: tests/git/scanner.test.ts — both tests fail today due to host environmental git config: 1Password's SSH/GPG agent fails to sign commits in temp repos created by simple-git. The scanner code is unchanged and the MVP gate (24/24) was green when the host wasn't using 1Password commit signing. Out of Phase 0 scope and accepted. Fix is to make the legacy tests resilient — e.g. set `commit.gpgsign=false` in the temp repo's local config, or pass `--no-gpg-sign` to `git commit` inside the test fixture.

tests/unit/main/ipc/system.spec.ts uses a dynamic import via string literal so the suite remains importable when the target module does not exist. Now that src/main/ipc/system.ts is committed and stable, this can be refactored to a static `import { handlePing } from '@main/ipc/system'` for better IDE support and to drop the @vite-ignore comment. Phase 1 cleanup.

electron.vite.config.ts uses externalizeDepsPlugin() for the main bundle, which means better-sqlite3 / @lancedb / find-git-repositories will be required from node_modules at runtime. Confirm electron-builder's asarUnpack rules (already in electron-builder.yml) cover all three before Phase 5 packaging. Not blocking for Phase 0.

Phase 1 should add an automated test that the production Electron build refuses to load a non-allowlisted file:// URL, locking in the sender-frame allowlist as a regression-tested behavior rather than only an inspectable property.

gate_decision.reason: Build, typecheck, and unit-test gates all green. Contract diff clean. End-to-end smoke confirmed: POST /api/scan streams NDJSON correctly, GET /api/repos returns canonical Repo shape with tags/languages/dirty/branch metadata, heuristic tagger detects rust/toml from Cargo.toml. The four LOW-severity issues are post-MVP polish, not blockers. The MEDIUM issue (FTS quoting) is a known refinement and does not violate the contract — falls back gracefully to empty results. MVP is shippable on branch build/repo-hub-mvp.

previous_gate.note: Preserved here because the Phase 0 report overwrites the MVP qa-report.json on disk. Do not lose this — the MVP backend is still on main and is still the production target until Phase 1 ships.

gate_decision.reason: Phase 0 is complete and shippable. Headline evidence: the Playwright Electron E2E PASSES (1 passed in 4.2s) — the launched app rendered 'pong' and surfaced a numeric mainProcessPid, proving the IPC contract works end-to-end through preload + contextBridge + main, not just at the schema layer. Phase 0 unit coverage is 44/44 green with 0 skips (35 schema + 9 IPC conformance), `pnpm electron:build` produces all expected artefacts (out/main/index.js 8.74 KB, out/preload/index.cjs 0.75 KB, out/renderer/index.html + assets), and both prior HIGH blockers (missing handlePing export, native-rebuild postinstall conflict) are resolved. The 2 scanner test failures are explicitly out of scope and accepted: they are host-environment flakes from 1Password's SSH/GPG agent breaking simple-git's temp-repo commits, the scanner code itself is unchanged from when the MVP gate scored 24/24, and the fix is legacy-test resilience (not a Phase 0 deliverable).
